newsitem.title: USA: Sprint President LeMay resigns to head Waste Management.
newsitem.headline: Sprint President LeMay resigns to head Waste Management.

text.p: Sprint Corp. said Monday that Ronald LeMay, its president and chief operating officer, resigned to become chairman, president and chief executive of Waste Management Inc. of Oak Brook, Ill.
William Esrey, Sprint chairman and chief executive, will assume responsibility for the positions that LeMay is vacating, the company said.
Waste Management announced LeMay's appointment in a separate statement.
Waste Management said Dean Buntrock, its founding chairman, will remain a member of the board, which is being expanded to 13 members with LeMay's election.
"Ron has been an outstanding leader for Sprint and a friend and trusted colleague to me personally," Esrey said of LeMay in a statement. "He will be greatly missed by all of us."

LeMay joined Sprint in 1985 as vice president and general counsel for the United Telephone System. He held several positions since then and was named president and chief operating officer of Sprint in February 1996.

"His strong track record, leadership and financial skills make Ron an outstanding choice to continue a disciplined focus on Waste Management's core business, its emphasis on cash flow generation and its commitment to shareholder value," Waste Management's Buntrock said.
Waste Management provides comprehensive waste management services.
